policies.title: Cameroonian and Chadian ordinary passports: Nigeria visa-free short visits
policies.summary: Nigeria's current consular visa-services table expressly places Cameroon and Chad under its visa-abolition agreement, each for up to 90 days. This direct agreement classification controls over a fee-table row.
conditions: The official table gives a maximum visa-free stay of 90 days. Ordinary admission, travel-document, health, security and border-officer requirements remain applicable.
The policy is limited to ordinary passports and a short visit. Employment, residence, transit, diplomatic, official, service, refugee and other special-document routes are outside scope.
Nigeria's positive F5A fee rows for these countries do not override the direct current visa-abolition classification.

policies.title: Barbadian ordinary passports: Nigeria F5A tourism eVisa
policies.summary: Barbados' current official travel schedule directly says its nationals require a Nigerian visa. Nigeria's current F5A route provides online, emailed certificate issuance for a non-waived tourist applicant.
conditions: The Barbadian official schedule confirms that the ordinary Barbadian visitor needs a Nigerian visa; its stated Nigerian High Commission route does not constitute an exemption.
For F5A tourism, apply online and receive the visa certificate by email before travel. The general F5A rules limit the stay to 30 days, single entry, within 90 days of issuance.
Mission procedures, work, residence, transit, diplomatic, official, service, special-document and final-admission treatment are outside this ordinary visitor baseline.

policies.title: Kenyan and South African ordinary passports: Nigeria F5A tourism eVisa
policies.summary: Nigeria's current reciprocity table confines the Kenya and South Africa waivers to diplomatic or official documents. Ordinary passports therefore use the current F5A tourism eVisa route, issued electronically before travel.
conditions: The Kenya and South Africa visa-waiver entries are expressly document-limited; they do not cover an ordinary passport.

Apply online under F5A tourism, upload the current required documents and obtain the visa certificate by email before travel. The route is single entry, tourism only, and allows up to 30 days' stay within 90 days of issuance.
Work, residence, transit, diplomatic, official, service, special-document and final-admission treatment are outside this ordinary visitor baseline.

application.label: Nigeria Immigration Service F5A tourism eVisa
steps: Apply online under F5A tourism with the ordinary Kenyan or South African passport.
Upload the required passport, return-ticket, accommodation and funds evidence.
Receive the visa certificate by email before travel and present it for carrier and admission checks.
